_comment: UNVERIFIED SEED DATA. domain -> normalized category. issuer_overrides encode the known disputes (e.g. Amex does not treat Instacart as a US supermarket). confidence: high|medium|low.

starbucks.com.note: reloads may code as dining, gift cards may not

instacart.com.note: third-party delivery; most issuers do NOT code this as a supermarket. barclays added 2026-09-28: the JetBlue cards' reward rules withhold bonus points from purchases made through third parties

target.com.note: classic trap: Target does NOT code as groceries on any major issuer

audible.com.note: Named in Prime Visa's 5% allowlist and missing from this table until 2026-09-10, which made that rule dead: audible.com resolved to no merchant, fell to `other`, and the card earned its 1% base. Category is online_retail because that is the rule the allowlist sits on, and because Audible sells digital goods. content_site is MEASURED 2026-09-10: the homepage carries Organization and FAQPage markup, og:type `book`, a price, no cart link and no buy control -- price only and nothing structural, which is the netflix.com shape, and one domain serves both the store and the player you listen in. Product pages carry Product and Offer, and commerce markup on the page beats content_site in isMerchantPage, so flagging darkens the homepage and the library while /pd/ pages and checkout still show. That is the opposite call from spotify.com for the opposite reason: Spotify's purchase surface has no markup to save it, Audible's does.

amazon.com.note: most cards have no online-retail bonus; expect the 2% catch-all to win

booking.com.note: Online travel agency, not a direct booking. Issuers that pay elevated rates only on 'booked direct' travel pay base rate here.

expedia.com.note: Online travel agency, not a direct booking. Issuers that pay elevated rates only on 'booked direct' travel pay base rate here.

airbnb.com.note: Online travel agency, not a direct booking. Issuers that pay elevated rates only on 'booked direct' travel pay base rate here.

netflix.com.note: measured 2026-09-09: no JSON-LD and no og:type on any surface, so only real payment machinery can tell the browse grid from the payment step

spotify.com.note: measured 2026-09-09 and deliberately NOT content_site: unlike netflix, spotify splits the surfaces. open.spotify.com (the player) carries no price and is already dark; spotify.com/us/premium/ is where you subscribe and should show. Flagging would suppress the second and gain nothing on the first. Latent risk: the player is dark only because price is false

hulu.com.note: measured 2026-09-09: same signal shape as netflix.com -- price only, nothing structural

disneyplus.com.note: measured 2026-09-09: no commerce markup, price only, and one domain serves both the marketing page and the signed-in browse grid -- the netflix.com shape

max.com.note: measured 2026-09-09: redirects to hbomax.com in a browser, so this row matches almost nothing now. Kept for stale links only

hbomax.com.note: measured 2026-09-09: the live HBO Max domain. Organization/WebSite markup, price only -- the netflix.com shape

youtube.com.note: only YouTube Premium/TV charges code as streaming

chargepoint.com.note: measured 2026-09-09: marketing home renders a price, so listing it mounts the dock there. Charging itself is paid at the charger; the web surface is account top-up

electrifyamerica.com.note: measured 2026-09-09: marketing home is signal-free, so listing costs nothing. Web surface is Pass+ plan signup

evgo.com.note: measured 2026-09-09: marketing home is signal-free. Web surface is plan signup

t-mobile.com.note: measured 2026-09-09: already showed via cart link + price, but ranked as everything else. Handset purchases here may code as retail rather than telecom

verizon.com.note: measured 2026-09-09: og:type article, no JSON-LD, price only. Same handset-vs-bill ambiguity as t-mobile.com. Split from phone_internet 2026-09-27 as phone: wireless is the bulk of what verizon.com bills, though Fios home internet is sold here too

xfinity.com.note: measured 2026-09-09: no JSON-LD, no controls, price only. Split from phone_internet 2026-09-27 as internet_cable: Xfinity Mobile is sold here too, but home internet and TV are the bulk of it

att.com.note: UNMEASURED: category assigned from the brand, signals not read off the live site. Filed as phone, not internet_cable: wireless is the bulk of what att.com bills, though AT&T Fiber is sold here too

spectrum.com.note: UNMEASURED: category assigned from the brand, signals not read off the live site

coned.com.note: measured 2026-09-09: public site is entirely signal-free, so the dock only appears once a bill page renders an amount due. Listed as the worked example -- see README on why a table cannot cover US utilities

staples.com.note: measured 2026-09-09: WebSite markup only, but a real cart link and a price, so it already showed -- as everything else, until this row

officedepot.com.note: measured 2026-09-09: Organization/WebSite markup, cart link and price. Covers OfficeMax, which redirects here

exxon.com.note: measured 2026-09-09: client-side redirect to exxonmobilfuels.com, so this row matches almost nothing now. Kept for stale links only

exxonmobilfuels.com.note: measured 2026-09-09: the live Exxon/Mobil consumer site. Rewards, station finder and both brand pages sit under it, and the Rewards+ account is on rewards.exxonmobilfuels.com, which the suffix walk covers. Home is signal-free; /en/rewards renders a price

hotels.com.note: Online travel agency, not a direct booking. Issuers paying elevated rates only on 'booked direct' travel pay base rate here.

priceline.com.note: Online travel agency, not a direct booking. Issuers paying elevated rates only on 'booked direct' travel pay base rate here.

vrbo.com.note: Online travel agency, not a direct booking. Issuers paying elevated rates only on 'booked direct' travel pay base rate here.

kayak.com.note: Online travel agency, not a direct booking. Issuers paying elevated rates only on 'booked direct' travel pay base rate here.

orbitz.com.note: Online travel agency, not a direct booking. Issuers paying elevated rates only on 'booked direct' travel pay base rate here.

travelocity.com.note: Online travel agency, not a direct booking. Issuers paying elevated rates only on 'booked direct' travel pay base rate here.

apple.com.note: Apple Card's 3% at Apple is merchant-scoped to this row, and the suffix walk carries it to every apple.com subdomain

nike.com.note: Footwear as much as apparel, so a shoe-store merchant code is as likely as a clothing one

dhl.com.note: The global DHL site; U.S. express shipping is booked here

ads.google.com.note: Measured 2026-09-27: signed out, this host redirects to business.google.com/us/google-ads/, which is marketing. Signed in it is the Google Ads app, where ads are bought and billed, so the row is live and redirects_to only keeps the sweep from reading the sign-in redirect as a move. An exact host, not google.com: nothing else on google.com is a merchant

business.facebook.com.note: Meta Business Suite, where ad billing lives. It also hosts page and inbox tools that are not purchases

adsmanager.facebook.com.note: Measured 2026-09-27: signed out, this redirects to the business.facebook.com login. Signed in it is Ads Manager, so the row is live; redirects_to only keeps the sweep from reading the sign-in redirect as a move

tjmaxx.tjx.com.note: T.J.Maxx's own site; tjmaxx.com redirects here. An exact host, so the rest of tjx.com -- the corporate site -- is not a merchant. Off-price apparel and home goods, filed as clothing, which is most of what it sells

marshalls.com.note: Same off-price shape as T.J.Maxx, and the same TJX Rewards card

homegoods.com.note: Home furnishings, which is the home_improvement bucket; a TJX Rewards store

homesense.com.note: Home furnishings; redirects to us.homesense.com, which the suffix walk covers. A TJX Rewards store

sierra.com.note: Outdoor clothing and gear; a TJX Rewards store

nordstromrack.com.note: Nordstrom's off-price chain, filed with its parent as a department store. Added 2026-09-28: the Nordstrom credit cards take 5% off here and earn no points.

ulta.com.note: Added 2026-09-28 for the Ulta cards. Cosmetics stores have no Caddy category, so the row sits in everything else. USAA Eagle Adapt's health and wellness rate names cosmetic stores, so that one card is understated here.
